neighbours.label: persistence of a past state into the present: the run-up to 'still / remains / to this day'
fire: Even now, centuries later, the villagers still speak the old dialect.
To this day the bridge carries traffic across the river.
Some courts still follow the procedure laid down in 1898.
The custom of lighting bonfires survives in a few valleys today.
Long after the war, the scars on the walls remain visible.
The family continues to live in the house their grandfather built.
Despite the reforms, the old law is still on the books.
Though the factory closed, its chimney stands to this day.
quiet: In those years the villagers spoke the old dialect at home.
In 1920 the bridge carried traffic across the river.
The courts followed the procedure laid down in 1898 for a decade.
The custom of lighting bonfires began in a few valleys long ago.
During the war, shells struck the walls of the town.
The family moved into the house their grandfather built.
After the reforms, the old law was repealed by parliament.
When the factory opened, its chimney was the tallest in town.

notes: Card: ' still' x4, ' remains', 'to this day the houses', 'survives in statute'; the + pole's output suppresses still/remains/retain, so this pole promotes them. Probe was weak (best 0.17 on 'Even today the old mill still...'). Near misses describe the same things in the past only.
